play.description: The Warriors' championship DNA shines brightest when they turn defense into instant offense. With the score knotted at 57 late in the second quarter at Chase Center, Steph Curry snatches a hard fought defensive board and amongst the scrum looks up court. The veteran forward finds Jimmy Butler streaking toward the rim, threading a perfect backwards, over-the-head pass that Butler finishes with a give-and-go running dunk. Golden State rode the momentum to a 120-97 blowout victory on December 22, 2025, with Curry contributing 26 points and 6 assists.

Steph Curry's legendary court vision isn't just about his shooting range, it's about creating opportunities for teammates in transition. Midway through the second quarter against the Clippers, Curry collected a defensive board and immediately pushed the pace, threading a perfect assist through the defenders legs to a streaking Will Richard who finished with an easy layup that stretched Golden State's lead. The Warriors dominated the October 28, 2025 matchup 98-79, with Curry orchestrating the offense beautifully for 19 points and 8 assists.

Forty-five seconds in and Steph Curry had already seen enough. With Green streaking ahead of the defense, Curry launched a full-court touchdown pass that hit his longtime running mate in perfect stride for the finger roll, the kind of connection that only comes from over a decade of shared basketball language. Curry finished with a season-high 11 assists, his 148th career game with 10 or more, as Golden State rolled 119-97.

The Golden State Warriors floor general has built a Hall of Fame career on long-range marksmanship, but Stephen Curry's finishing package remains elite. On Christmas Day against the Dallas Mavericks, the veteran guard attacked the rim with purpose. Curry navigated through the defense, absorbed contact, and floated in a delicate layup off the glass to keep Golden State's offense humming. Though the shot itself is not one you typically see in Curry highlight reels, this shot hit a little different. This bucket gave Steph his 26,000th career point - just the 25th player in NBA history to hit that mark. The two-time MVP finished with 23 points on 6-of-18 shooting in the 2025 Christmas Day contest.

There is no “preferred time” for opponents to ever go head-to-head against Stephen Curry, but if 16 years of NBA history has confirmed anything, it’s that 29 franchises should hope to avoid drawing one specific calendar date: February 27. Chronicled already for a 53-point “arrival”-type performance in 2013, the infamous double “bang” in Oklahoma City in 2016, and a 50-point showpiece in 2018, Curry eyeballs his next victim, starting by adjusting his sights to a quite-fitting 51-foot buzzer-beater. By that point, the Golden State Warriors found themselves in a 14-point halftime hole, but a message to the NBA’s No. 1-ranked defense had been sent. History’s most celebrated sniper dedicated the next two quarters to verifying precisely why, using a 35-point (on 14 shot) exhibit to begin the Warriors’ climb back, a journey that ultimately closed in victory. Approaching something close to his Most Valuable Player-winning levels over the post-All-Star break stretch, Curry’s greatness against the Orlando Magic encouraged 56 points, four rebounds, three assists, and two steals. Closely behind were double-take-worthy marks from the field (16-of-25), from deep (12-of-19), and from the charity stripe (12-of-12), prompting a 15th 50-point game, and a 32.6-point scoring average on said date.

With a pair of MVPs and four titles under his belt, it’s hard to know what’s next for Steph Curry. Turns out more of the same. Racking up 29.4 points per game on his best shooting numbers in a half-decade, Curry’s 2022-23 campaign signaled just how much gas is left in the 35-year-old’s tank as the Golden State Warriors set out to repeat as champions.

Come at the king, you best not miss. In this one, Steph Curry puts his handles to work as he crosses up Dillon Brooks before hitting his defender with a pump fake and drilling a silky three-pointer. But if that wasn't enough, Curry celebrated all the way down to the floor, feigning disbelief for his heroics. The greatest shooter in NBA history wrapped the game with 24 points, 7 boards, and 6 assists as the Golden State Warriors took down the Houston Rockets in this matchup from October 29, 2023.

Stephen Curry has built a Hall of Fame career on shots that demoralize opponents, and he added another chapter with 26 seconds remaining. Protecting a slim lead on January 7, 2026, the Warriors guard sized up his defender near the right elbow before creating separation with his trademark stepback. The 22-footer found nothing but net, pushing Golden State's lead and punctuating Curry's efficient 31-point, 7-assist masterpiece in a 120-113 victory at Chase Center.

Seemingly inspired by the NBA’s recent, historic scoring binge, Steph Curry decided it was time to welcome himself to the 60-point party. Right at home during a fast-paced, nip-and-tuck affair against the Atlanta Hawks, the former two-time NBA Most Valuable Player put in the second-highest scoring game of his illustrious career as only he could: 3-pointers from every area of the hardwood, subtle attacks to the rim whenever the defense assumed it had cracked the code, and perhaps most impressively, only six free throws. The Golden State Warriors would ultimately be topped in overtime, but not without top-tier theatrics from the 10-time All-Star. Unable to be contained, Curry lit up the scoreboards for 60 points and 10 three-pointers — only the third player in NBA history to hit those two marks —  along with six rebounds, four assists, and a block on February 3, 2024.

Two-and-a-half weeks before the 2025 NBA Playoffs began, 16-year superstar Stephen Curry took to his postgame presser, uttering five words that should’ve perked the ears of every Western Conference contender: “The tank is pretty full.” Using it to fuel the Golden State Warriors’ Game One road win, No. 30 unleashed the full checklist on April 20, 2025. Unconscious trifectas from the Houston Rockets’ sidecourt logos. Geometrically-unfair, shot-clock-beating 3-pointers, all the while falling out of bounds; if it could be done, Curry forced the unsupporting Texas crowd to ensure it during the series opener. The final play-by-play tallied Curry for five different 3-pointers of 25+ feet away, planting the seeds for a 31-point, six-rebound, three-assist, one-steal finish on rock-solid efficiency overall (12-of-19), from deep (five-of-nine), and from the foul line (two-of-two). Riding the wave of their “Splash Brother,” the Warriors cruised to a statement-sending Game One win, immediately stealing home court advantage against a common foe.

Steph Curry’s shooting and scoring abilities get their just praise — but how about some love for the way the Golden State Warriors star gets his buckets? Granted an opportunity to strike from the corner, Curry sets his sight on the rim, splitting two defenders with a smooth behind-the-back maneuver, then finishes at the cup with a layup. The four-time champion scores two of his game-high 24 points on the play while also chipping in six rebounds, 10 assists, two steals and five triples in his squad’s 111-101 win on November 18, 2022.

Down 20 points with playoff seeding on the line, Steph Curry and the Golden State Warriors never panicked. The nine-time All-Star stayed calm under pressure despite being face-guarded by CJ McCollum, and with Curry unable to get his own shot off he did the next best thing — whipped a pass to Klay Thompson, who buried the catch-and-shoot 3-pointer. Curry’s dish capped a huge final frame for the Warriors, who outscored the New Orleans Pelicans by 15 in the period and turned the huge deficit into a 120-109 win. Curry posted 39 points, eight rebounds, eight assists, three steals and an 8 for 15 mark from downtown on March 28, 2023.

As he found the bottom of the net on a stop-and-rise triple that upped his point total to 49, Stephen Curry —  in the greatest zone of his young career —  high-stepped into a dance towards the floor’s opposite end, oblivious to even the teammates seeking to join his celebration. Not that he should’ve felt bad; as the New York Knicks attempted to swarm him with every defensive strategy possible, Curry hadn’t noticed them, either. Having seemingly reached the doorstep to greatness in 2012-13, the Golden State Warriors star entered Madison Square Garden on February 27, 2013 intent on officially kicking it down. In leaving the road crowd audibly confused on what emotion to feel, Curry offered a precursor of what the ensuing decade would entail: crafty, high-arc releases at the rim, 3-pointers from every angle and launch point, and answers for every defender one could send his way. Down their All-Star big, Golden State entrusted Curry with a full 48-minute workload, and he responded demonstratively, even in defeat. Meeting the challenge against the NBA’s scoring champion and the East’s No. 2 seed, Curry rained in 54 points (on 18 of 28 shooting), six rebounds, seven assists, and 11 3-pointers.

Steph Curry never has been one to shy away from putting his legendary range on display. In a rematch of the 2022 NBA Finals against the Boston Celtics, a Golden State Warriors possession ended with a Curry turnover before the nine-time All-Star quickly redeemed himself by picking Jayson Tatum’s pocket on the counterattack. With the second quarter clock hurtling toward zero, Curry only had time to loft a prayer from beyond halfcourt that of course landed in the bottom of the net. Curry posted a team-high 29 points in the overtime battle while adding four rebounds, seven assists, three steals, two blocks and six 3-pointers on January 19, 2023.

For the ninth time in his legendary 14-year career, Steph Curry found himself on an All-NBA squad. The Golden State Warriors sharpshooter earned his fourth Second Team selection to go with four First Team berths and another on the Third Team after averaging 29.4 points per game, the third-highest output of his career. Also an All-Star for the ninth time, Curry became the Warriors’ all-time leader in field goals made during the season, and also became the first player in NBA history to score at least 10,000 points off of 3-pointers. In his 56 games played, he recorded at least 30 points in 28 of them, including four 40-point performances and two more in which he posted 50. Curry is now tied for the most 50-point games in league history after the age of 30 with seven, and his 50-point effort in Game 7 of the Western Conference Semifinals was a playoff career-high and briefly the most points ever scored in a Game 7 until Jayson Tatum bested it by a single point shortly thereafter.

Every on-court appearance for No. 30 of the Golden State Warriors, as viewers can attest, includes the opportunity at seeing a never-before-seen on the NBA’s hardwood. In front of Philadelphia’s nationally-televised audience on March 1, 2025, Stephen Curry pivoted his focus to arguably the next best thing: a type of bucket he hadn’t produced in over a half-decade. Driven, perhaps, by the spirit of the fearless Philadelphia 76ers legend he paid tribute to upon arrival, Curry turns back the clock in transition, elevating for his first in-game throwdown since February of 2019. Challenged by his assistant coach, and doubted by his head coach at once, Curry — given only a “50-50” chance of successfully finishing the jam — silenced nearly every skeptic during this year’s trip through the City of Brotherly Love. A 44-point breakout by Philadelphia’s equally-ambitious sniper played spoiler here, but Curry was nonetheless brilliant, chalking up 29 points (on 10-of-18 shooting), five rebounds, 13 assists, one steal, and five triples.

A decade-and-half into mastering the art of making the faraway appear close, and the seemingly-impossible appear easy, Stephen Curry confirmed for all who might’ve been curious that yes, over-the-head, full-court skyhook passes are also embedded into his long-range arsenal. Blending together an eye-opening highlight tape before some had even found their seats at Smoothie King Center, the Golden State Warriors superstar engulfs a rebound, all the while maintaining his downfloor teammate’s fastbreak position in his peripheral. In a maneuver that would’ve brought a smile to the NBA’s No. 2 leading scorer, Curry puts torque on a hooking, over-the-body dime that perfectly falls into his teammate’s grasp, setting up a jaw-dropping assist. Accuracy, in nearly every way, was the name of the game for Curry, as he tallied 19 points, seven rebounds, seven assists, one steal, one block, and four 3-pointers. Such efforts helped Golden State survive a nail-biter, clinching West Group C through a victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on November 22, 2024.

It takes a special type of atmosphere to leave a player with six NBA Finals appearances, three gold medals, and a 16-year professional incapable of explanation. Yet, as Stephen Curry processed seeing his 11-year “Splash Brother” shooting on —  as he called it — the other end of “the blacktop at recess,” one inevitable, competitive challenge remained: reminding the NBA world of who Golden State’s playground belongs to. Fueled by the adrenaline of a Chase Center already in mid-eruption, Curry takes his crunchtime artistry to a place exclusive to almost him, hunting out a pick-and-roll switch against Dereck Lively II. Authoring an ever-special moment, even after having done it thousands of times, Curry captures another unforgettable sequence, breaking free of the Dallas Mavericks center through a crossover before elevating into a game-clinching, goosebumps-inducing triple, accompanied by a trademark “Night Night” celebration. Curry’s greatness arrived in different layers, the last of which arriving by scoring the Golden State Warriors’ final 12 points to seal a once-improbable come-from-behind victory. The ultimate superstar on November 12, 2024’s emotional night, Curry’s final tally read as follows: 37 points (on 14-of-27 shooting), six rebounds, nine assists, one steal, two blocks, five 3-pointers, and a +24 plus-minus.

Down by five points with 17 seconds left in a playoff game is a bad place to be — unless Steph Curry is on your side. In his first MVP and championship season, the Golden State Warriors icon flashed some of his patented brilliance in crunch time in Game 3 of a first-round postseason series against the New Orleans Pelicans. The Warriors trailed by 20 heading into the final period before mounting a furious rally, capped off by a pair of Curry 3-pointers in the final 11 seconds, with the first coming on the preceding Golden State possession. Now down three with nine seconds on the clock, Curry grabbed an inbound pass from Draymond Green in the corner before misfiring on a triple that would have tied the game on the spot. Luckily for fans of the nascent dynasty, Marreese Speights snared the offensive board and handed the ball back to Curry for another corner triple that broke the raucous home crowd’s heart. It marked the first time in 359 tries during the shot clock era that the Warriors won a game in which they trailed by 20 points entering the fourth, and they had Curry’s 40 points to thank for it. Curry also finished with five rebounds and nine assists in the thrilling 123-119 overtime victory on April 23, 2015 and his club finished off the sweep two nights later.

Stephen Curry reminded San Antonio why he's the greatest shooter ever to lace them up. In a close battle at Frost Bank Center, the Warriors point guard unleashed his full offensive repertoire - from a patented stepback triple to a crafty driving floater that kissed the glass. He capped this highlight reel with a finger-roll layup through traffic, threading the needle with his trademark touch around the rim. Chef Curry cooked up 49 points on 16-26 shooting (9-17 from deep) in the 109-108 thriller on November 14, 2025.

Doomed, somewhat by an ice-cold shooting start that left them behind on the scoreboards throughout the game’s first three quarters, the Golden State Warriors, in their attempt at stealing momentum, couldn’t have picked a more poetic shot choice. Smooth and unassuming in his dribble, Stephen Curry sees the respect of his long-range shooting legacy in play, with both Rudy Gobert and Nickeil Alexander-Walker itching to contest whatever rainbow shot will arrive within the following seconds. Presented with just the sliver of space needed to let a shot fly, Curry elevates into a buzzer-beating 39-foot moonball, bringing Chase Center to its feet as only he can. Curry’s fellow Hall of Fame-bound teammate took care of any “nite-nite” celebrations for him a quarter later, as Golden State ultimately found success in exacting revenge from a loss just two nights prior. Plenty electric, even in Year 16, Curry concluded with 30 points (on 8-of-18 shooting), four rebounds, eight assists, one steal, and five 3-pointers on December 8, 2024.

Fully established into his spot as the 2023-24 NBA season’s No. 1 scorer with the game hanging in the balance and the clock operating against him, Steph Curry certainly wasn’t one to complain about having time to plan his heartbreaker against the Oklahoma City Thunder. Afforded the luxury of navigating his steps with 15 seconds remaining in a tied, high-scoring affair, the former two-time Most Valuable Player eases closer to the basket, like predator attacking prey before subtly using a between-the-leg dribble to escape Lu Dort’s defense. Free to glide into the lane, Curry uses finesse, hanging a high-arching finger roll out just out of Chet Holmgren’s reach on the way to a game-winning bucket. Curry’s heroics provided the Golden State Warriors with a second-consecutive at-the-buzzer victory, allowing them to open the In-Season Tournament in memorable fashion on November 3, 2023. The 10-time All-Star dazzled throughout with a game-high 30 points, eight rebounds, seven assists, two steals, and five 3-pointers.

Steph Curry has built a Hall of Fame career on impossible shots that feel inevitable in his hands. With less than one minute remaining in the fourth and the Warriors nursing a slim lead on the road in Los Angeles, who else gets the ball but Curry? His shot? One that only Steph would not just take, but bury. From 35 feet out, Curry squares up without hesitation and puts the opening-night duel on ice.

From their now-shared “Night Night” celebration to the methods in which they influence one another’s scoring, it’s worth suggesting that after 13 shared seasons, Stephen Curry and fellow title-raising teammate know one another’s movements before they even happen. Testing the theory during an early-game ball screen against the New York Knicks, Curry disattaches himself of Miles McBride before freezing in his tracks around the free throw area to re-analyze the defense. Knowing the lack of a roll to inevitably mean a pop, Curry unleashes a nonchalant-as-can-be behind-the-back assist to his eagerly-awaiting wingman, setting up an uncontested 3-point bucket. Two days after making NBA history through 4,000 3-point makes, Curry’s accuracy — as both a shooter and facilitator — remained spot on during March 15, 2025’s win. Unphased by relatively-low scoring numbers on both sides, the Golden State Warriors’ megastar stood out through a 28-point contribution (on 8-of-20 shooting), accompanied by seven rebounds, five assists, one block, and four 3-pointers.

When Steph Curry starts catching fire, there isn’t much that opposing defenses can actually do about it. Against the LA Clippers in this one, the four-time Golden State Warriors champion hit the 50-point threshold for the 12th time in his legendary career. Curry showed off his patented lightning-quick release from downtown as he torched the Clips for 8 triples in 14 tries, hitting step-back jumpers over Paul George, Ivica Zubac and anyone else the defense sent his way. Curry also showed off his evasive handles in attacking the lane, blowing by Zubac with an ankle-breaking maneuver that led to an underhand scoop shot. Curry also utilized a spin move that gave him enough space to stick a tough baseline fadeaway and proved elusive enough to split a pair of Clippers defenders on a strong drive to the bucket that resulted in a well-earned layup. An All-Star for the ninth time in 2023, the two-time MVP shot 20 of 28 for 50 points — 21 in an explosive third quarter — and also mixed in six assists and two steals on March 15, 2023.

Steph Curry did not have to wait very long to pump himself and the Golden State Warriors up. In the second game of his 14th NBA season, the nine-time All-Star lost control of the ball on the perimeter before handing it off to Kevon Looney. Looney dumped it down low to Draymond Green, who immediately flicked a pass to a cutting Curry for a driving layup that had him mugging for the baseline camera in celebration. It was the second of three straight 30-point games to open the 2022-23 season for Curry, who posted 34 points, five rebounds, four assists and five 3-pointers against the Denver Nuggets on October 21, 2022.

In securing a win that left his Golden State Warriors just a half-game back of the Los Angeles Lakers’ No. 9 seed, Stephen Curry found that the recipe was quite simple when it came to shaking up the Wild West Play-In picture: merely allowing his team’s offensive possessions to play out. Having left the Lakers’ head coach to describe his Warriors as “blazing, blazing hot” in his post-game assessment, the former two-time Most Valuable Player prepares a pass attempt of equal superlative. First working an evasive dribble down the right baseline, Curry unleashes an underhanded missile just out of reach of Rui Hachimura’s panicked frame, and right into the hands of his cutting teammate for a backdoor find and selfless score. Winners of eight of their last nine, Golden State matched their scorching game-by-game streak with a historic heatwave, connecting on 26 3-pointers and NBA history’s highest single-game percentage for a team with at least 40 attempts. Leading the charge, Curry took his always-efficient ways a step further, requiring just nine shots to accumulate 23 points, seven rebounds, eight assists, one steal, two blocks, and a perfect six-of-six from distance in April 9, 2024’s win.

New season, same old Steph Curry daggers. Locked in a tie ballgame late in the fourth against a feisty Sacramento Kings squad, the Golden State Warriors’ four-time champion makes it known that he is not interested in an overtime session. Curry takes his time setting up the halfcourt offense before burying a 28-foot stepback to give his squad a lead it would not relinquish. The eight-time All-Star poured in 47 points — 17-for-24 from the field and 7-of-12 from downtown — along with eight rebounds and eight assists in Golden State’s 116-113 victory on November 7, 2022.

Who else would the Golden State Warriors turn to with their season on the line? In a win-or-go-home Game 5 of the Western Conference semifinals, Steph Curry brought his squad back from the brink of elimination with a patented clutch performance. The four-time champion willed the Warriors to victory, getting the best of Lonnie Walker IV in an isolation matchup by using his evasive handles to create enough space to pull the trigger on a 3-pointer that beat the halftime buzzer. One of Curry’s three triples gave the Warriors an 11-point advantage at the break, and his game-high 27 points and eight assists delivered a 121-106 triumph over the Los Angeles Lakers on May 10, 2023.

Another season, another milestone-packed masterclass from Stephen Curry.

In Year 16, the Warriors icon was named to his 11th All-NBA Team after averaging 24.5 points, 6.0 assists, and 4.4 boards on elite shooting splits—44.8% from the field, 39.7% from three, and a league-best 93.3% from the line. He passed 25,000 career points and became the first player in league history to eclipse 4,000 made threes, adding fresh fuel to an already untouchable legacy.

Curry’s signature game came in a February shootout vs. Orlando, where he dropped 56 points and hit 12 threes, igniting Chase Center and basketball fans everywhere. He was as dangerous off movement as ever, bending defenses nightly with his gravity, IQ, and clutch shotmaking. Still the face of Golden State, still rewriting the record books—Curry’s greatness isn’t slowing down.

Twelve seasons in, the two-time MVP found another gear, as if his usual one wasn’t already unstoppable. In his sixth game of a season where he would claim a second scoring title, Curry dismantled the Trail Blazers defense from every level: 20 points from inside, 24 from beyond the arc, and 18 from the charity stripe. That night in Chase Center, Curry not only dropped a career-best 62 points, but also became the first player since Pistol Pete in ‘77 to score 30 in each half.

No matter the situation, Steph Curry has the ability to leave jaws dropped every time he touches a basketball. The Golden State Warriors left everybody in the arena speechless when he snared a pass from Andrew Bogut on the perimeter and instantly ran into a wall of defensive traffic. Undeterred by the heavy pressure, Curry dribbled around his back through a trio of Clippers before stepping behind the arc and abruptly unleashing an off-balance 3-pointer from the top of the key that somehow swished. In the first of his two straight MVP seasons, Curry scored just 12 points on nine shots yet still left the arena as the most talked about player on the floor. The circus shot even left head coach Steve Kerr — who made 726 3-pointers and shot better than 45 percent from downtown during a 15-year NBA run — in total disbelief. Curry added four assists and three steals in Golden State’s 106-98 victory on March 8, 2015 and would later go on to win his first championship later that year.

Although four months remain until the Golden State Warriors play host of the NBA’s 2025 All-Star Weekend, the 18,000-plus in attendance can be rest-assured of Stephen Curry’s night-to-night creativity keeping them at bay. Turning a third quarter back-and-forth against the L.A. Clippers into a mid-game Skills Challenge course, the 10-time All-Star channels youthful hustle during a mad loose ball scramble, volleying it skyward to prevent Ivica Zubac’s retrieval. Met by a “final boss” of sorts with James Harden pursuing a charge and Derrick Jones Jr. pressuring his path, Curry maximizes creativity and control, steering through California traffic with a behind-the-back and eventually, an acrobatic reverse finish. Los Angeles would command the last laugh through an eight-point win on October 27, 2024, though Curry, in Year 15, remained perfectly in electrifying form. Despite ultimately being sidelined by an ankle injury, the always-efficient floor general dazzled nonetheless with 18 points (on 6-of-11 shooting), four rebounds, six assists, and four triples in 27 minutes.

In his first home game following a long injury absence, Steph Curry gave the fans -- including 55 Top Shot collectors from the Strength in Moments fan community -- their money's worth. An All-Star for the ninth time in 2023, Curry was especially clutch in the fourth quarter and overtime against the Milwaukee Bucks, hitting three huge 3-pointers in the final two minutes of regulation, including one that tied the score with 19 seconds left. Curry then preserved the tie and sent the game to the extra session when he landed a critical block on Jrue Holiday's driving layup attempt. Of course, Curry wasn't done as he nailed an overtime trey that put the game out of reach — his 36 points, six rebounds, four assists, two steals and six triples guided the Golden State Warriors to a 125-116 win on March 11, 2023. The four-time champion became the all-time Warriors leader in field goals made in 2023 while also tying an NBA record with his seventh 50-point game after the age of 30.

Missed shot attempts seldom make one’s highlight reel, particularly ones in the game’s opening minute. But, as Stephen Curry raced the floor, eager to introduce the NBA’s fastest-paced team to its perfect deep-range complement, the make-or-mess result mattered much less than the underlying message: the Association’s new fearless, limitless sniper had officially arrived. A game-changing offensive hub from his career’s literal first play, Curry — with an added step or five behind the 3-point line in future seasons — immediately demonstrated what would someday solidify his Hall of Fame candidacy. Accurate on anything leaving his hands, be it a trademark pull-up or a pass to keep the Golden State Warriors’ team-first offense energized, Curry’s debut proved memorable, especially during a 12-point, six-of-six shooting flurry during a final-quarter comeback attempt against the Houston Rockets. Unknowing of his starting role until hours before October 28, 2009’s tip-off, Curry electrified nonetheless, capturing 14 points (on 7-of-12 shooting), seven assists, and four steals (three in the first seven minutes). Wearing the “Curry” name proudly in creating league history’s 24th-ever father-son tandem, the No. 7 pick set the rookie pace as the Rookie of the Year runner-up, with every award his imagination could conjure arriving years later.

From taking the No. 1 spot on the NBA’s single-season 3-point leaderboard to guiding his Golden State Warriors to NBA history’s best-ever 58-game start, Stephen Curry’s shooting on February 27, 2016 left no record incapable of being broken. But as the clock ticked down, with the last shot of his timeless performance closely approaching, the soon-to-be two-time Most Valuable Player broke something of a different kind: the Oklahoma City Thunder’s spirit. Successfully generating a stop with six seconds remaining and a timeout at their disposal, the Warriors enter the game’s most consequential possession with options aplenty. Fusing a flawless blend of fearlessness and never-before-seen accuracy, Curry refuses the timeout, instead easing his dribble past the Thunder’s midcourt logo before splashing a 32-foot game-winner, capping off one of basketball history’s greatest shooting exhibits. One game removed from a 51-point masterpiece, Curry’s response evoked similar goosebumps as he finished with 46 points — 12 over the five-minute overtime span —  six assists, two steals, and a then-record-tying 12 3-pointers. In sending his message to a fellow Western Conference title contender, Curry shook off an injury scare to send the Warriors to a 53-5 start, momentum they would ultimately ride to the 2016 NBA Finals.

Already one of the last players that teams want to see in crunch time, “Chef Curry” has turned the pressure cooker on his late-game brilliance up a few notches in 2023-24. Far and away this season’s leader in both clutch points and field goals, Steph Curry adds to the extensive evidence, spinning to retrieve a pinpoint inbounds pass from his teammate and then matching its accuracy with a cold-blooded, game-settling triple. Playing to the crowd, the Golden State Warriors superstar put on a consistent show, upstaging the Phoenix Suns with 30 points, nine rebounds, six assists, and nine 3-pointers in the victory on February 10, 2024.

Goosebumps-including atmospheres and must-see moments can be found across the NBA’s globe, but on their absolute best day, they would have a difficult time topping what Stephen Curry and Chase Center created side-by-side on March 13, 2025. One trifecta shy of becoming NBA history’s first to hit 4,000 3-pointers, Curry — likely feeling the murmurs and anticipatory energy of the crowd — inadvertently loses his handle, prompting a diving, multiplayer scrum for a loose ball. Finding that to be somewhat of a disguised blessing, Curry turns it into a reasonable look, pump-faking Trey Lyles out of position before relocating, setting the stage for a triple of record-breaking proportions. In what merely became the latest example in Curry’s case as basketball’s most celebrated long-range sniper, the suddenly-hot Golden State Warriors rode the wave of momentum to win No. 11 over a 12-game span. Not necessarily needing to pair his milestone-crossing night with a big-time scoring output, Curry tallied 11 points (on nine shots), alongside two rebounds, five assists, one steal, one block, and a 3-pointer in a win over the Sacramento Kings.

In the second game of a young 2025 NBA season, the greatest shooter in basketball history reminded everyone why that title remains undisputed. Curry poured in 42 points against Denver, punctuated by a trio of clutch three-pointers late that not only forced overtime and sent Oracle Arena into pandemonium, but also delivered an early statement victory. The 7th pick in the 2009 NBA Draft, four-time NBA champion, and two-time MVP displayed the lethal combination of deep range, quick release, and unshakeable confidence that has defined his Hall of Fame career. Even at this stage of his journey, Curry continues to deliver vintage performances that blur the line between art and athletics, proving that his gravitational pull on defenses and his ability to bend games to his will remain as potent as ever.

Steph Curry hoops on a different plane of existence while the rest of us take notes. After casually strolling past half-court and into his effective range, the NBA’s most potent deep threat draws three Philadelphia 76ers defenders, steps back into an effortless triple, then signals to the Chase Center crowd that he’s feeling it in a way that only he could. Curry finished the November 24, 2021 contest with 25 points, 10 dimes and a Golden State Warriors victory.

Golden State Warriors superstar Steph Curry has naturally creative instincts as a passer, with the patience and skill to improvise and make a pinpoint dime. He scoops up an errant feed, takes a slight dribble and lofts a beautiful, two-handed, over-the-head dish to a wide open Jordan Poole for a breakaway slam. Curry dropped a game-high 10 assists to go along with 24 points, six rebounds and three steals in a road matchup against the Charlotte Hornets on November 14, 2021.
